Security review of PR 650 showed the text floor is bypassable (sh -c quoting, gh api, curl, update-ref) and that containment was not real: the sandbox allowed network, passed exported tokens, exposed ~/.config/gh-work, shared a writable /tmp, was skipped silently when no launcher existed, and the health gate ran agent-written code with no sandbox at all. The floor stays as defence in depth; the boundary moves to a mandatory, hardened sandbox.

Security review of PR 650: containment was not real (network on, exported tokens and ~/.config/gh-work visible, shared writable /tmp, sandbox skipped silently without a launcher, health gate ran agent code unsandboxed) and spend could go unrecorded (killed runs, providers without streamed usage, concurrent triggers each seeing the full allowance, zero rates). These criteria make the boundary and the budget contractual.

Security review of PR 650: a killed run left its worktree registered to the trigger branch, so every later fire failed at git worktree add with exit 1 forever.
